name: Residential Electrical Contractors
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For residential electrical business owners. Clarify electrical contracting versus low-voltage cabling or smart-home installation. Explore their workflow, then explain Answering Service, Receptionist and Manager in order. These conditional examples establish no qualifications, compatibility or active capabilities. Recommend the lowest useful level; consult shared pricing for costs.
discovery_questions: Is your main work residential electrical service, installations or a different specialty?
Which types of calls interrupt your team most often?
What happens when someone calls while everyone is at a job?
What details does your office need before accepting a request?
Which requests can be booked directly, and which need an electrician's review first?
Where do you currently keep appointments and customer requests?
Who should handle complaints or requests outside your approved service scope?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved hours, service-area and accepted-work questions without assessing installations or interpreting electrical requirements.
Collect contact details, property location and the caller's estimate or service request for human review.
Send a reason-for-call summary to one agreed destination while the crew is unavailable, preserving the office's control over scheduling.
levels.probe: Would consistent request capture be enough, or does the caller need another step during the call?
fit_signals: Missed calls and incomplete voicemail details are the main problem.
A qualified person must review every job before scheduling.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify inquiries using owner-approved service-area and work-category rules and offer screened transfers through configured human destinations.
Use one standard calendar integration for approved consultation or estimate slots if the business permits direct booking for those request types.
Alternatively, use one standard CRM integration to capture qualified inquiries for staff review; this choice does not also include calendar booking.
levels.probe: Would approved appointment booking or CRM lead capture remove more office work for you?
fit_signals: The office repeatedly checks the same intake criteria.
There are documented eligibility and handoff rules for common requests.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Collect detailed complaints about a prior service experience and the requested resolution for an authorized human, without deciding fault.
Explain approved estimate, appointment-change and follow-up policies while sending exceptions and financial questions to the business owner.
Coordinate approved escalation routes and potentially support both a calendar and CRM within two standard integrations total, subject to compatibility and scope.
levels.probe: Which follow-up calls need clearer escalation rules?
fit_signals: Repeat policy questions or complaints consume owner time.
The defined workflow needs two confirmed integrations.

scope_boundaries: Level 1 excludes booking, CRM integrations and screened transfers. Level 2 includes one standard calendar OR CRM integration; Level 3 includes two total, not two additional integrations.
Do not diagnose electrical hazards, provide DIY wiring or repair instructions, interpret code compliance, certify safety or promise that a described job is suitable.

For an immediate safety concern, stop the sales discussion and refer at a high level to appropriate local emergency services or a qualified human. Do not troubleshoot or instruct the caller to test equipment.
No promised emergency response, dispatch, arrival, price, refund, discount or policy exception. Human financial and technical decisions remain with the business; examples do not perform live actions.
setup_requirements: Confirm business specialty, approved work categories, service area, hours, FAQs and one summary destination.
Document what may be booked, what requires technical review, calendar permissions and staff transfer or escalation availability.
Confirm compatible systems, the chosen integration count and fallback behavior; approve and test the configured call paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: Office staff manually move the same inquiry between tools.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separately scoped intake workflow with approved actions and human exception handling.

adjacent_services.trigger: The owner says the website does not explain accepted work or capture inquiries.
adjacent_services.example: Discuss clear service pages and an inquiry form based on the business's actual service scope.

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: We are residential electricians and get interrupted by estimate calls.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Level 1, Answering Service, could collect request details and send one summary for your review. What do you need to know before deciding the next step?

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: The location and kind of work, then we arrange an estimate.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Level 2, Receptionist, could qualify those details and support screened transfers, with either approved calendar booking or CRM lead capture. Can estimate visits be booked without an electrician reviewing them?

example_conversation.speaker: caller
example_conversation.text: Some can, but complaints always come to me.

example_conversation.speaker: agent
example_conversation.text: Level 3, Manager, could gather complaints, explain approved policies and escalate exceptions, with two integrations total. You retain financial decisions. Which part of that would save you the most time?
